default: always on -- a query surface. Nothing here can change emitted C, so no phases.toml row, no options.rs registration and no catalog counter (docs/agents.md: the option rule is scoped to behaviour that CAN change emitted C).
decisions: The filed hypothesis -- 'reads starting in mapped memory appear to zero-fill an unmapped suffix' -- is upheld and is the upstream BFD contract, not a kuna defect: LoadImageBfd::loadFill (ported at kuna-analysis/src/loadimage_object.rs) fills a 512-byte buffer forward from the requested address and, once ANY byte has been read, zero-fills to the next segment instead of failing. That is what makes a .bss tail read back as zeroes rather than as a hole, so it must not change: the decompiler, the analysis tier and every reader depend on it.

The refuter's sharper wording is the one that held: this is a MISSING END-CLIP, not a zero-fill policy. The containment guard in listing_for is applied to region.start only (prog.vma_bytes_mapped), and nothing ever bounded the length. The fix therefore lives entirely in the query surface, which is why the need was retracked quality -> tooling before dispatch.

The bound is the contiguous mapped RUN, not the containing segment. Clipping at a segment edge would truncate a listing that crosses from one PT_LOAD into the next at the byte the first ends -- a real ELF layout, and one that reads through today. mapped_run merges adjacent and overlapping records first, so only a genuine hole stops the walk.

A loader that publishes no segments at all (the XML <binaryimage> corpus loader, a relocatable object -- both return an empty get_segments) yields no bound and the walk is unchanged. Silence is not evidence of an unmapped image, and treating it as one would have emptied every corpus listing.

The straddle is half the defect and was not in the filed symptom. At the last mapped byte the translator still decodes a 2-byte `add [eax],al` out of one real byte and one zero-filled one; stopping the LOOP at the bound does not stop THAT row from claiming a byte past it. A decoded row that would cross mapped_end is refused the way a translator refusal is, so the mapped bytes under it list as .byte. The whole-corpus sweep found this is in fact the ONLY thing that changes on already-good images -- 11 of 11 changed listings are that one row.

truncated stays false. Its documented contract is 'there is more to list, and `end` is where to resume from' -- true for the 1024-row derived cap, false at the end of the image, where resuming at `end` errors. The stop is carried by `notes` instead (present in --json and on stderr), which is also the field the tester said was empty.

kuna read had the same defect (384 zeroes across the gap under a header claiming the range) and is the same walk, so it is fixed by the same clip; walk_data's read_upto could never shorten because load_fill never fails there.

Green under `env -u KUNA_DECOMP_TEST` (4/4). This change touches only kuna-cli and cannot reach a kuna-decomp oracle. CI does not export the variable.

speed.note: No measurable cost: the clip is one get_segments() call and a merge over the segment list (2 records on a typical ELF, tens on a PE), once per invocation, outside the decode loop. The per-row cost is one Option compare.

sweep.method: A/B of `kuna decompile-graph`'s per-function `assembly` blocks (the same walk `kuna disassemble` uses, via disassemble::function_listing) between the base commit's kuna and the patched one, over every function of every image.
sweep.classification: 11 of 11 are the same single row: the final instruction of a function whose extent reaches the end of a mapped section, previously a fabricated 2-byte `ADD byte ptr [EAX],AL` half of which was zero fill, now `.byte 0x00`. Row counts are IDENTICAL in every case -- no listing was truncated and no row was lost anywhere in either corpus. Witnesses: pe_imports.exe register_frame_ctor@0x140007a10, upx_packed_pe_i386.exe sub_4100a0@0x4100a0, illusion.exe, CTF_Level13.exe, TBMKD.sys.
sweep.not_covered: The windowed (--count / --bytes / range) path is not reachable from decompile-graph; it is covered by the acceptance probe, the promoted tests/cli case and the two disassemble_cli.rs e2e tests.

acceptance.promotion_note: The dataset witness is 6.5 MB, so the promoted probe is re-pointed at the vendored 4.3 KB segmentgap_i386 fixture (CI has no dataset) -- same layout, same failure: unfixed it answers end 0x804803f with 22 invented rows.
